newsitem.title: KUWAIT: ATHLETICS-KUWAIT THREATENS PARTIAL ARAB GAMES BOYCOTT.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-KUWAIT THREATENS PARTIAL ARAB GAMES BOYCOTT.

text.p: Kuwait have threatened to boycott any events in next month's Pan Arab Games in Beirut involving competitors from its former occupier Iraq, newspaper reports said on Tuesday.
The al-Seyassah newspaper said Sheikh Ahmad al-Fahd al-Ahmad al-Sabah, chairman of the Kuwait Olympic Committee, announced Kuwait's "intention to withdraw" from any event involving an Iraqi athlete.
"Kuwait's team would be present at the opening ceremony where players will carry pictures of Kuwait POWs (prisoners of war) held at Iraqi prisons," he said.
Iraq and Kuwait are among 20 countries taking part in the July 12-27 event.
Kuwait says Iraq, which invaded the Gulf Arab state in 1990 and occupied it for seven months, still holds some 600 Kuwaitis. Iraq denies this.
In Beirut, Games organisers said they hoped Kuwait would not be caused any embarrassment by Iraq's participation.
Zeid Khyami, a director-general at the sports ministry in charge of organising the games, said: "We will handle the issue in the interest of Kuwait.
"We want Kuwait to participate in the games in a manner that will preserve Kuwaiti dignity, the dignity of the games and the success of the event," he added.
Lebanon has no diplomatic relations with Iraq but has close ties with Kuwait.
Kuwait and Saudi Arabia have contributed substantially to the $50 million cost of building the 50,000-seat Beirut stadium at which many of the Pan Arab Games' events will be held.
The two countries have also contributed financially to many other Lebanese reconstruction projects.
